_purpose: Seed authority-policy fixtures. These are examples/defaults, not a claim that ForgeWorld already had production-grade permission rules for these capabilities -- it did not; only capabilities/registry.json (reachability) and prose governance/*.txt existed before this mission. Every decision here is deliberately conservative: no policy in this file grants an autonomous agent broader authority than the NRM incident already demonstrated (branch-write yes, tag-publish no).

policies.reason: Observed evidence (NRM incident): a non-force branch push succeeded with session credentials. Bounded to non-force pushes; which specific branches are additionally protected (e.g. main) is enforced by the remote's own branch-protection rules, not duplicated here -- see docs/governance/AUTHORITY_MODEL.md for why this policy does not re-implement that as a second, possibly-inconsistent local rule.
Creating an annotated/lightweight tag object in the local repository never touches the remote; no external trust boundary is crossed.

Direct observed evidence: `git push origin NRM-v0.1-CLASSROOM` returned HTTP 403 on the same remote and credentials that had just accepted a branch push. Publishing a tag ref is a distinct, more restricted operation on this remote. See docs/evidence/NRM_TAG_403_CASE.md.
Fixture default. No deployment platform integration currently exists in this repository; conservative default until one is defined and a human sets explicit policy.

Promotion is defined (see promotion.py) as independent of execution success. No amount of passing build/test/device evidence may substitute for a human promotion decision. Matches this mission's explicit instruction: promotion remains human-controlled.
Fixture default. Bounded to an explicit allow-list that starts empty -- no channel is pre-approved by this mission. A human must populate approved_channels before any autonomous send is possible.

Fixture default matching the mission's Support-agent example ("may execute refunds <= threshold, must escalate above threshold"). max_amount defaults to 0 -- effectively no autonomous spend authority -- until a human sets a nonzero bounded threshold.
Fixture default. Deletion is not reversible by this runtime's existing tooling (no soft-delete/undo primitive found), so it defaults to requiring approval.

Self-protection rule required by this mission (section 16): no agent may edit authority rules to grant itself or any other agent broader authority during execution. See delegation.guard_self_escalation().
Agent creation is not authority creation (mission section 15). Granting authority to a new or existing agent is itself an authority-modifying act and inherits MODIFY_GOVERNANCE's HUMAN_ONLY posture.
Fixture default. Same blast-radius tier as PROMOTE_RELEASE and PRODUCTION trust boundary; no autonomous path exists in this repository today, so none is created here.

Added for FORGEWORLD PERCEPTION GATEWAY PROOF 001: a CapabilityProposal (perception/src/schema.py) may never self-promote into the Knowledge Vault -- 'models may propose relationships but may not validate them' is a mission constraint, and this policy is what makes evaluate_authority() actually deny an agent-actor attempt at PROMOTE_KNOWLEDGE rather than the rule existing only in prose. Same blast-radius posture as PROMOTE_RELEASE: no autonomous path exists.

Added for FORGEWORLD DYNAMIC CAPABILITY DISPATCH INTEGRATION MISSION (FW-CAP-DISPATCH-004): an isolated, reversible sandbox probe of a fully-verified, unique-gap capability candidate never touches a remote system or crosses an external trust boundary by definition (see capability_dispatch/src/dispatch.py's UNBOUNDED_EXECUTION_SURFACE gate, which independently blocks any candidate requiring network+shell+credentials before this policy is even consulted). This mission itself grants no THIRD_PARTY_INSTALLATION_AUTHORITY or PRODUCTION_PROMOTION_AUTHORITY -- this policy only ever lets the dispatch engine assign the SANDBOX_PROBE disposition to a candidate; it never authorizes installing, cloning, or actually executing anything (see capability_dispatch/THIRD_PARTY_SAFETY_BOUNDARY.md).

Added for FW-CAP-DISPATCH-004. Installing a third-party capability is the mission's named highest-severity gate (13 pre-installation requirements, mission Section 13) -- this policy is what makes evaluate_authority() actually deny an autonomous attempt rather than the rule existing only in prose. No capability_dispatch code path currently calls evaluate_authority for this capability at all (this mission grants no installation authority to exercise), so this policy is a forward-looking fixture only, matching PROMOTE_RELEASE's and PROMOTE_KNOWLEDGE's identical posture.
